channel.title: x402 Blog — AI agent micropayments

item.title: OpenClaw 2026.7: a ready config with ASI1, Ollama, and free OpenRouter models
item.description: A working openclaw scaffold for 2026.7.x: local Ollama, cloud ASI1, free OpenRouter models, and MCP servers for trading and web research. Secrets are placeholders only.

item.title: An agent without memory is an intern who comes to work for the first time every day
item.description: Not intelligence, but lack of continuity is the most underestimated agent problem. Four levels of memory, the cost of bad memory, and why memory is architecture, not a mechanism.

item.title: OpenClaw + Pionex: how to build a cron agent for automated trading via MCP
item.description: A cron agent on OpenClaw, Pionex MCP, cron, and Telegram: scheduled PERP scanning, active-bot checks, signal selection, and futures grid creation. The system's key rule — knowing when not to trade.

item.title: Why the fastest companies to $100M ARR are now agentic
item.description: Agentic companies reach $100M ARR noticeably faster than classic SaaS. The reason is product form: an agent closes a whole slice of work instead of augmenting a human. The price of speed is autonomy, control, and observability.

item.title: The agent economy is no longer theory: who pays, who earns, and where the real volume is
item.description: Three contours of the agent economy: executors inside businesses, agents selling services, infrastructure. Who pays, who earns, and why micropayments stop being exotic.

item.title: The agent that beat humans: how autonomous systems are already earning six figures
item.description: Xbow, Cursor, Clay and solo founders: autonomous agents are already generating six-figure revenue. Breaking down the money loop an agent closes without human involvement.

item.title: Humans should no longer be the executor
item.description: While agents were weak, humans stayed as the main executors. With growing autonomy, the role shifts — from doing the work to orchestrating: goals, constraints, verification points.

item.title: The main problem with agents is not intelligence — it's reliability
item.description: Models have gotten smarter, but the main reason agents aren't in production isn't about IQ. It's about reliability. Step-by-step failures, trust, and what really holds agents back.

item.title: What actually makes an agent different from a chatbot
item.description: Most people still confuse AI agents with advanced chatbots. The difference is not in the quality of answers — it's in how they work. Planning, tools, memory, feedback loops.

item.title: Why most companies haven't launched agents in production yet
item.description: Less than 10% of companies have reached meaningful AI agent usage. The demo-to-production gap, lack of control, economics, and organizational barriers. What's stopping them and how to fix it.

item.title: Multi-agent systems grew 327% in four months. What this actually means
item.description: Databricks: multi-agent systems grew 327% in 4 months. 78% of companies use models from 2+ families. 97% of test and dev DB environments are created by agents.

item.title: How much code agents already write (and why it matters more than it seems)
item.description: By 2026, Claude Code generates a noticeable share of GitHub commits. Inside companies, 30–40% of new code is written by agents. What this changes in development and why task formulation becomes the key skill.

item.title: Agents already broke production. And it was inevitable
item.description: An Amazon agent shut down AWS in China for 13 hours. Another destroyed a database in 9 seconds. Real cases, lessons and protection.

item.title: Agents already work 12 hours without humans. And this is just the beginning
item.description: AI agent autonomy horizon grew from 40 minutes to 12 hours in a year and a half. METR data, growth curve and what this changes in practice.

item.title: What it actually costs to run an agent (and why most calculations are wrong)
item.description: The real cost of an AI agent isn't just token prices. Tools, errors, oversight, risks — the full cost picture and why you should measure cost per outcome, not cost per request.
